about: Failure patterns of a whole flow that no single place shows. The scanner matches each one's structure over a recorded flow (version 2); the scenario author writes at least one scenario per matched pattern, HARMLESS when it does not bite. Reliability wording only.

ack-before-durable.name: Answered before the work is durable
ack-before-durable.hypothesis: The caller is told the work was accepted while part of it exists only in memory or in an open transaction; a crash then loses it and nobody asks again.
ack-before-durable.questions: Which effects of this entry point are not durable when the answer goes out? Who would notice their loss, and would the caller retry?
ack-before-durable.stepFix: persist the pending work in the same transaction before answering
ack-before-durable.conceptFix: make the answer depend only on durable state: an outbox or a work table that a job drains
ack-before-durable.verify: Stop the JVM right after the answer; after a restart every accepted effect must still happen.

external-effect-inside-local-tx.name: External effect inside a local transaction
external-effect-inside-local-tx.hypothesis: An effect in another system (a charge, a message, an account) is made inside a local transaction; a rollback afterwards cannot undo it, and a retry repeats it.
external-effect-inside-local-tx.questions: Is the external effect reversible or idempotent by a key? What happens to it when the local commit fails? Does a retry or redelivery make it again?
external-effect-inside-local-tx.stepFix: send an idempotency key with the external call
external-effect-inside-local-tx.conceptFix: record the intent with a client-generated key and commit it before calling out, then complete the local state from the result
external-effect-inside-local-tx.verify: Make the local commit fail after the external call succeeds; the external effect must not be repeated by the retry, and the local state must be repaired.

fan-out-without-outbox.name: One transaction tells several systems
fan-out-without-outbox.hypothesis: One transaction sends to or calls more than one other system; a failure between them leaves some told and some not, with nothing to finish the rest.
fan-out-without-outbox.questions: Can any of the sends or calls fail after another succeeded? Which side would see the inconsistency, and is there a reconciliation?
fan-out-without-outbox.stepFix: mark each target as done in the database and retry the ones not done
fan-out-without-outbox.conceptFix: write all outgoing messages to an outbox in the transaction and relay them after the commit
fan-out-without-outbox.verify: Make the second target fail after the first one succeeded; every target must eventually agree.

at-least-once-without-idempotent-sink.name: Repeated delivery reaches a sink that repeats
at-least-once-without-idempotent-sink.hypothesis: Work arrives by at-least-once delivery (a broker or a retried webhook) and ends in a write or call that has no duplicate check, so a redelivery repeats it.
at-least-once-without-idempotent-sink.questions: When does the sender deliver again (timeout, error, crash before the ack)? Which write or call repeats, and does anything key it by the message or event id?
at-least-once-without-idempotent-sink.stepFix: store the message or event id with a unique constraint in the same transaction as the work and skip duplicates
at-least-once-without-idempotent-sink.conceptFix: key every effect down the chain by one business id that each hop checks
at-least-once-without-idempotent-sink.verify: Deliver the same message twice, and twice at once; the effect must happen once.

uncorrelated-callback.name: Callback that cannot be matched to its request
uncorrelated-callback.hypothesis: A call to an external system is answered later by a webhook or callback, and nothing stores the request's id where the callback handler looks it up, so a callback cannot be matched, is applied twice, or arrives for a request that failed.
uncorrelated-callback.questions: What id does the external system send back? Does the outbound side store it before calling? Does the callback handler look it up before acting?
uncorrelated-callback.stepFix: look the callback up by the stored external id and ignore unknown or repeated ones
uncorrelated-callback.conceptFix: store a pending request with its external id before the call, and let the callback move it to its final state
uncorrelated-callback.verify: Send the callback twice, and once for a request whose local commit failed; each must be handled once or rejected visibly.

callback-before-commit.name: Callback arrives before the local commit
callback-before-commit.hypothesis: The external call is made inside a transaction that commits after it; the external system can answer by webhook before the commit, when the row the callback needs is not visible yet.
callback-before-commit.questions: How fast can the callback come? What does its handler do when the row is missing: fail and get redelivered, or drop the event?
callback-before-commit.stepFix: make the callback handler fail with a retryable status when the row is missing
callback-before-commit.conceptFix: commit the pending state before calling out, so the callback always finds it
callback-before-commit.verify: Delay the local commit and deliver the callback first; it must be applied once the commit lands, never lost.
